title: Personal Finance explained
description: The government has kept interest rates for popular small savings schemes unchanged for July-September 2026. This means stable returns for schemes like PPF, SC.

faq.a: Small savings schemes are government-backed investment options offered through post offices and some banks in India, designed to promote saving among citizens by providing secure and often tax-efficient returns.

faq.q: Who decides the interest rates for these schemes?
faq.a: The interest rates are decided by the Ministry of Finance, Government of India, during a quarterly review.

faq.q: Are these rates guaranteed for my entire investment period?
faq.a: It depends on the scheme. For SCSS and NSC, the rate is locked for the tenure of your investment. For PPF and some Post Office deposits, the interest rate can change quarterly, and your account earns the prevailing rate.

faq.q: Which are the most popular schemes right now?
faq.a: PPF, Senior Citizen Savings Scheme (SCSS), and Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY) are among the most popular due to their safety, competitive interest rates, and tax benefits.

faq.q: Do these schemes offer tax benefits?
faq.a: Yes, many small savings schemes, including PPF, SCSS, NSC, and SSY, offer tax benefits under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act for investments up to ₹1.5 lakh annually. The interest earned on PPF and SSY is also tax-free.
